extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of gasoline distribution facilities, industry stakeholders, state and EPA regulators, and public commenters (legal and technical advisors)
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule preamble and rationale for EPA's Technology Review (CAA §112(d)(6)) and NSPS review (CAA §111) for gasoline distribution and bulk gasoline terminals, describing regulatory requirements, emissions limits, monitoring, and compliance definitions applicable to major and area sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: RIA analysis years and timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial analysis year in the RIA is 2027 (majority of impacts begin then); final analysis year is 2041 to present 15 years of projected impacts after rule take-effect; compliance with existing source standards occurs 3 years after promulgation (hence 2027).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for projecting costs, emissions reductions, benefits/disbenefits across 2027–2041; tables present PV and EAV monetized benefits, compliance costs, and net benefits for that period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discounting rates for benefits and disbenefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate disbenefits are discounted using a 3 percent social discount rate; all other impacts presented use social discount rates of 3 and 7 percent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetization and present-value calculations should apply these discount rates as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost analysis methodology (model plant + facility projections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost analysis reflects a nationwide engineering analysis of compliance cost and emissions reductions using (1) representative/model plants for each regulated facility, segment, and control option, and (2) projections of data for affected facilities distinguished by vintage, year, and necessary attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impacts are calculated by setting parameters on how/when affected facilities respond, multiplying data by model plant cost and emissions estimates, differencing from baseline, summing to aggregation level; present projected compliance costs with and without revenues from product recovery where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability — source categories and NAICS guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: This action applies to Gasoline Distribution regulated under 40 CFR part 63, subparts R and BBBBBB, and Bulk Gasoline Terminals regulated under 40 CFR part 60, subparts XX and XXa; 2022 NAICS codes 324110, 493190, 486910, and 424710 provided as a guide (not exhaustive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities should examine the applicability criteria in the appropriate NESHAP and NSPS and consult contacts listed for applicability questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: CAA §112 two-stage standard-setting (MACT and residual risk/technology review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 112 establishes a two-stage process: (1) promulgate technology-based standards (MACT) and (2) evaluate MACT-based standards via residual risk review to determine if additional standards are needed; EPA also must review standards every 8 years for developments in practices/processes/control technologies (technology review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technology review pursuant to CAA §112(d)(6) is required for all standards under §112(d), including GACT; EPA may consider costs when deciding to revise standards; not required to recalculate MACT floors during technology review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of major vs area source (emission thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Major source: emit or have potential to emit 10 tons per year (tpy) or more of a single HAP or 25 tpy or more of any combination of HAP. All other sources are area sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different requirements apply to major vs area source categories (MACT for major, GACT option for area).

rubrics_metrics.name: MACT standard requirement and MACT 'floor'
rubrics_metrics.description: For major sources, §112(d)(2) requires MACT standards reflecting the maximum degree of emission reductions achievable (considering cost, energy, and nonair health/environmental impacts). §112(d)(3) establishes a minimum control level (the MACT 'floor').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must consider control options more stringent than the floor (beyond-the-floor standards) as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: GACT standard allowance for area sources
rubrics_metrics.description: For area source categories, §112(d)(5) allows EPA to promulgate standards requiring use of generally available control technology or management practices (GACT) in lieu of MACT; EPA can consider costs/economic impacts in determining GACT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GACT development evaluates control technologies and management practices generally available for the area source category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 112(k)(3)(B) urban HAP identification and goal
rubrics_metrics.description: §112(k)(3)(B) requires EPA to identify at least 30 HAP that pose the greatest potential health threat in urban areas with the primary goal of achieving a 75 percent reduction in cancer incidence attributable to HAP from stationary sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA implemented this via the Integrated Urban Air Toxics Strategy (identifying the '30 urban HAP').

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 112(c)(3) listing obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: §112(c)(3) requires EPA to list sufficient categories/subcategories of area sources to ensure area sources representing 90 percent of emissions of the 30 urban HAP are subject to regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implemented through the Integrated Urban Air Toxics Strategy and subsequent listings (including Gasoline Distribution).

rubrics_metrics.name: NSPS review frequency and BSER standard (CAA §111)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §111(b)(1)(B) EPA must review and, if appropriate, revise NSPS at least every 8 years (unless Administrator determines review not appropriate). Performance standards should reflect the degree of emission limitation achievable through application of the Best System of Emission Reduction (BSER), taking into account cost, nonair health/environmental impacts, and energy requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA determines BSER and degree of emission limitation achievable; §111(b)(5) generally precludes prescribing a particular technology; §111(h) allows work practice standards where measurement/feasibility issues exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSPS 'new source' and 'modification' definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to §111(a)(2), standards apply to facilities that begin construction, reconstruction, or modification after publication of proposed standards. §111(a)(4) defines 'modification' as any physical change or change in method of operation that increases the amount of any air pollutant emitted or results in emissions of a pollutant not previously emitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 40 CFR 60.15, 'reconstruction' means replacement of components where fixed capital cost of new components exceeds 50% of the cost to construct a comparable new facility and it is technologically/economically feasible to meet applicable standards. Changes that do not result in emissions increases are not modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: NESHAP Subpart R — loading rack TOC limit (existing requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Emissions from loading racks at major source gasoline terminals under NESHAP subpart R are required to be controlled by a vapor collection and processing system to meet a TOC emission limit of 10 mg/L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls must achieve the TOC emission limit; EPA proposed retaining this limit for new and existing sources in subpart R.

rubrics_metrics.name: NESHAP Subpart R — gasoline cargo tank vapor-tight certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Gasoline cargo tanks must be certified to be vapor tight using a graduated vapor tightness requirement of 1.0 to 2.5 inches of water pressure drop over a 5-minute period, depending on the cargo tank compartment size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA proposed reducing allowable pressure drop to 0.5–1.25 inches in the proposed rule; final action likewise revises vapor tightness for major and area sources to be more stringent.

rubrics_metrics.name: NESHAP Subpart R — storage vessel control thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Emissions from storage vessels with a design capacity ≥75 cubic meters must be controlled by equipment designed to suppress emissions (internal or external floating roof meeting certain requirements) or must capture and control emissions to a device achieving 95 percent reduction efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative compliance is allowed via capture and control to 95% reduction efficiency; proposed additional fitting requirements for external floating roofs and LEL monitoring for internal floating roofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: NESHAP Subpart R — equipment leaks LDAR
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment leaks are subject to a leak detection and repair (LDAR) program using monthly inspections to identify leaks via audio, visual, or olfactory (AVO) methods and repair the leak identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA proposed semiannual monitoring using OGI or Method 21 in addition to AVO for identified leaks; final revisions include instrument monitoring for equipment leaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: NESHAP Subpart BBBBBB — TOC loading rack limits and size thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: For area-source terminals: loading racks at terminals with throughput ≥250,000 gallons per day must reduce TOC to ≤80 mg/L; small bulk gasoline terminals (20,000–250,000 gpd) and bulk gasoline plants (≤20,000 gpd) must use submerged filling with submerged fill pipe ≤6 inches from bottom of cargo tank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA proposed reducing the large terminal limit from 80 mg/L to 35 mg/L and providing VRU-equivalent concentration limits; final rule revises standards under technology review.

rubrics_metrics.name: NESHAP Subpart BBBBBB — gasoline cargo tank vapor-tightness
rubrics_metrics.description: Gasoline cargo tanks must be certified to be vapor tight using a maximum allowable pressure loss of 3 inches of water pressure drop over a 5-minute period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA proposed tightening to 0.5–1.25 inches depending on compartment size.

rubrics_metrics.name: NESHAP Subpart BBBBBB — storage vessel control thresholds and fixed-roof requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: At bulk gasoline terminals and pipeline breakout stations, storage vessels with design capacity ≥75 m3 and throughput >480 gpd and all storage vessels ≥151 m3 must be controlled by floating roofs or capture & 95% control; storage vessels below thresholds must have fixed roofs and maintain all openings closed when not in use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These thresholds determine which vessels need active vapor suppression vs simple closure practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: NESHAP Subpart BBBBBB — equipment leaks LDAR
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment leaks at all area source gasoline distribution facilities are subject to an LDAR program using monthly AVO methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA proposed annual monitoring with OGI or Method 21 for additional detection and repair requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSPS Subpart XX (existing) — loading rack TOC limits and applicability window
rubrics_metrics.description: NSPS subpart XX regulates VOC emissions (as TOC) from bulk gasoline terminals that commenced construction/modification/reconstruction after December 17, 1980 and on or before June 10, 2022; TOC emission limit for loading racks is 35 mg/L, except modified affected facilities with an existing vapor processing system (as of Dec 17, 1980) must meet 80 mg/L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cargo tanks must be certified vapor tight with maximum allowable pressure loss 3 inches water over 5 minutes; equipment leaks subject to monthly AVO LDAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSPS Subpart XXa (proposed/final) — loading rack TOC limits for new/modified/reconstructed sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed limits: for thermal oxidation systems, 1.0 mg/L for new bulk gasoline terminals and 10 mg/L for modified/reconstructed terminals; for VRUs, corresponding concentration limits proposed of 550 ppmv and 5,500 ppmv TOC (as propane) to be equivalent to 1.0 and 10 mg/L, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA finalized these standards in NSPS subpart XXa but included an allowance to exclude methane from measured TOC (i.e., non-methane TOC effective limits). Facilities may choose to comply using direct TOC measurements without methane correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow methane subtraction from TOC emission limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule includes provisions to exclude the contribution of methane from the measured TOC emissions, making the final emission limits effectively non-methane TOC limits (e.g., 1.0 mg/L non-methane TOC for new sources; 10 mg/L for modified/reconstructed sources), while allowing facilities to comply using direct TOC measurements without methane correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This amendment reflects comments and ensures limits reflect non-methane hydrocarbon content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring methods and frequencies (OGI, EPA Method 21, AVO, instrument monitoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring provisions vary by rule: existing LDAR uses monthly AVO; proposed/final changes include semiannual monitoring using OGI or Method 21 (NESHAP subpart R proposed), annual monitoring using OGI or Method 21 (subpart BBBBBB proposed), and quarterly monitoring using OGI or Method 21 (NSPS subpart XXa proposed). EPA is also finalizing instrument monitoring for equipment leaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaks identified by these monitoring events or by AVO must be repaired; monitoring frequency and method depend on source category and subpart provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vapor balancing requirement for bulk gasoline plants over throughput threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed: require vapor balancing between gasoline cargo tanks and gasoline storage vessels for bulk gasoline plants with capacity over 4,000 gallons per day; final rule uses actual throughput (with annual averaging) rather than maximum design capacity to determine applicability of the 4,000 gpd threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Threshold determination changed in response to comments to reflect actual daily throughput averaged annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pressure relief valve opening pressure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed for subpart BBBBBB: require pressure relief valves on fixed roof tanks to have opening pressures set to no less than 2.5 pounds per square inch gauge (psig).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to limit unnecessary venting and emissions from pressure-relief actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal floating roof LEL concentration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed: for storage vessels with internal floating roofs, maintain concentrations of vapors inside a storage vessel above the floating roof to less than 25 percent of the lower explosive limit (LEL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures effectiveness of internal floating roofs and safety; EPA finalized LEL monitoring to ensure effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of separate affected facilities in NSPS subpart XXa
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalizes two separate affected facility definitions: (1) 'gasoline loading rack affected facility' — 'the total of all the loading racks at a bulk gasoline terminal that deliver liquid product into gasoline cargo tanks including the gasoline loading racks, the vapor collection systems, and the vapor processing system' (loading rack emission limits apply here); and (2) 'collection of equipment at a bulk gasoline terminal affected facility' — 'all equipment associated with the loading of gasoline at a bulk gasoline terminal including the lines and pumps transferring gasoline from storage vessels, the gasoline loading racks, the vapor collection systems, and the vapor processing system' (ensures equipment leak provisions apply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design separates applicability so that adding tank farm equipment does not trigger loading rack control requirements, but does trigger equipment-leak requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thermal oxidation systems continuous compliance requirement (NSPS XXa)
rubrics_metrics.description: For thermal oxidation systems, continuous compliance with a temperature operating limit established as the lowest 3-hour average temperature from a compliant performance test was proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes enhanced provisions for flares to ensure good combustion efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: VRU dilution prevention (vacuum breaker limitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed: to prevent dilution, only vacuum breaker valves can be used to introduce ambient air into the VRU control system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures VRU monitoring and concentration limits remain representative and enforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of SSM exemptions in NESHAP
rubrics_metrics.description: This action finalizes the removal of startup, shutdown, and malfunction (SSM) exemptions in the NESHAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emissions limits clarified to apply at all times; SSM exemptions removed to ensure continuous applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic reporting and other technical improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Final action includes electronic reporting, monitoring and operating requirements for control devices, and other minor technical improvements; emission limits revised/clarified to apply at all times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment summaries and responses for issues are in docket; for all comments not discussed in preamble see comment summary/response document in docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalency of mg/L and ppmv TOC limits for VRU-controlled systems
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA provides concentration equivalents for VRU-controlled loading racks: e.g., 5,500 ppmv TOC (as propane) determined equivalent to 10 mg/L; 19,200 ppmv equivalent to 35 mg/L; and 550 ppmv equivalent to 1.0 mg/L (used for NSPS XXa equivalencies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA proposed expressing VRU concentration limits on a 3-hour rolling average to be enforceable with VRU monitoring systems; equivalencies used to allow alternative control technologies.
